before: That completely threw me. Fights don't usually go like that. Anger is a way to get more power when you feel a lack of justice or agency. You puff yourself up so you seem frightening or dangerous, or you demand to be heard. My anger was there to get me heard, and her answer showed me I didn't need it for that. Whatever injustice I thought there was wasn't coming from a lack of love, either. So the anger seemed stupid. I saw for myself that it was only hurting me, without helping me see clearly or get what I wanted. Still, what I screamed was true right then, and what she said back was true too, so I could hate somebody who loved me and she'd still be my mom the whole time.

guide_passage: Don’t turn the sentence into a formula. “But I love you” can become dismissive when it means, “Therefore stop being angry.” The useful test is whether the love can remain alive, hear the anger, and take whatever is true in it seriously. Non-retaliation is one expression of love; it is not a colder substitute for love.
